about: The airport weather marks on the map (the owner's pick, 2026-11-10): a field's least crosswind on its runways (least_crosswind), whether its wind earns an arrow and whether the arrow is red (wind_arrow), the station model's barb (wind_barb, FAA-H-8083-28B 25.2.3.4.5), and the getting-worse badge, a route field's METAR now against its TAF for the flight's time there (weather_worse, AIM 7-1-7). Read by the engine's tests (engine/facade/tests/weather_marks.rs), the web's (lib/map/marks/airportWeather.test.ts) and the phones'.

leastCrosswind.why: 220 at 18 gusting 26 over 18/36 and 27/09: 40 degrees off runway 18, the gust's 26 sin 40 = 16.7, 17 kt; 27 leaves more (50 degrees off).
A runway's number turned true with the variation where its end has no true heading: 36 with 10 degrees east is 010 true, so a wind from 010 is straight down it.
A variable wind may blow straight across any runway: all of it, the gust's 15 kt, is crosswind (AIM 7-1-28).
A field with no runway end to judge the wind on (a heliport's H1) has no figure.

windArrow.why: 6 gusting 16: an arrow for the gust.
17 kt across against a 15 kt demonstrated crosswind: red.
Exactly the demonstrated crosswind is not more than it.
No airplane picked, or no figure for it: never red, nothing assumed.

windBarb.why: 2 kt rounds to 0, the circle (the NWS table: 0-2 kt is 0).
3 kt is 5, a half-barb alone (the NWS table: 3-7 kt is 5).
65 kt: a flag, a barb and a half-barb.

worseByArrival.why: KDLH VFR now, its TAF IFR for the flight's time there: the badge.
KMSN IFR now and better by then: no badge.
KRST VFR now and VFR by then, a lower ceiling still VFR: no badge (worse than VFR only).
